places.name: Hỏa Ngọc Mạch
places.size: A volcanic island about 12 km long and 5 km wide, the cone some 1,400 m high, with a second small islet beside it; the only human trace is a guarded camp of about 10 huts and a landing for alchemists and miners on short tours.
places.where: Region 1, far out in the western sea off the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác. On the map a long dark island with a steep cone and a second summit, a second small islet to the east, deep blue open sea all around. Volcano; a spirit vein of fire jade (Fire, Water) charted by Thúy Vi, 224 km from Tịch Chiếu Đảo. Few ships come.
places.imagined: Dusk over a black cone in a dark sea. Seams of fire jade glow red-green through the rock down the flanks like a cracked lamp, steam leaks from the crater, and a single small ship lies at the landing.
places.subject: The place: Hỏa Ngọc Mạch, the Fire Jade Vein, a steep black volcanic island far out in a deep western sea. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; the island lies in the middle of the frame, long and narrow, a steep black cone rising from it with a second lower summit, ringed by a narrow rim of black sand, white surf and pale turquoise shallows, the open deep blue sea filling the rest to every edge, with a small green islet in the upper right. The cone: black basalt, scored with ravines, a thin steam plume from the crater and wisps leaking from fissures on its flanks, pockets of dark green scrub low on its sides. Signature element: branching seams of fire jade, glowing red and green through the dark rock, run down the cone's sides like veins of molten glass, some of them kilometres long, brightest where they cross, with faint haloes of heat-shimmer along the ridges. Human trace: on a sheltered black-sand cove at the southern foot, a small guarded camp of about ten plain timber huts with grey roofs, a stone landing with one two-masted ship at anchor, a switchback mule track climbing toward the lowest seam, a few tiny figures with picks and baskets, a lookout post; nothing else. Light and season: dusk in late autumn, golden light from the upper left on the cone's western face, the sea in cool blue shadow, the jade seams glowing against the darkening rock, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Hỏa Hồ Nguyên
places.size: A tundra plain of the cape at true scale: a broad flat expanse tens of kilometres across with about 30 fox dens, each a thawed patch 10-30 m wide; no buildings, no camp.
places.where: Region 1, tundra of the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác at about 140 m. On the map a rugged brown-grey tundra of hummocks and scree on the left, a dark blue inlet and a green coast to the right. Beast lair, fire foxes (yêu cốt prize). Far from other lairs: Hàn Tượng Nguyên 348 km. Belongs to no sect.
places.imagined: A low sky and a flat white plain. Round brown pockets of thawed earth dot it like coins, each with a dark den hole, trails of melted prints running between them, and one fox as a bright orange speck.
places.subject: The place: Hỏa Hồ Nguyên, the Plain of the Fire Foxes, a vast flat white tundra on a cold cape. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; a broad flat expanse of white tundra snow fills the frame, low lichen-covered hummocks breaking it, a frozen stream bed winding across it as a pale blue-grey line, rough grey scree ridges at the left edge and a dark inlet of the sea with a rim of ice at the far right edge. Signature element: scattered over the plain, about thirty round pockets of bare thawed brown earth, each some ten to thirty metres across, each with a dark round den hole at its centre and a halo of wet dark ground, so that they read as coins thrown on a white cloth; between them run thin trails of melted footprints, brown dotted lines in the snow, linking dens in loose chains, and near the largest patch the snow has melted back in a wide ring and steam rises from the den. A few tiny fire foxes, bright russet-orange specks with pale tails, sit or run on the snow, one at a den mouth, one crossing the frozen stream. No buildings, no huts, no camp, no people. The air above the den pockets shimmers faintly with warmth, and the snow edging each pocket is grey and slushy. Light and season: low late-winter sun from the upper left under a thin high cloud, warm golden light on the snow with long soft blue shadows from the hummocks falling to the lower right.

places.name: Tuyết Để Tuyền
places.size: A high snowfield about 2 km across with one blue ice cave at its foot, about 30 m wide; no buildings, at most a tiny bottling hut and a cairn.
places.where: Region 1, high mountain of the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác, about 550 m. On the map a small rocky dark peak on an island with a green island beside it, in a bright sea, snowfield on the upper slopes. Hot spring (linh tuyền thủy; Fire, Water) held by Thúy Vi. Nearest: Hắc Diệu Khoáng mine 79 km.
places.imagined: Dawn on a smooth bright snowfield. One blue cave mouth breathes a thick plume of white steam, a warm green stream runs from it across grey stones, and tiny figures bottle water at its edge.
places.subject: The place: Tuyết Để Tuyền, the Spring beneath the Snow, a hot spring in a high mountain snowfield. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a smooth, bright, steep snowfield fills the upper two thirds of the frame, unmarked except for faint wind ripples and a few long shallow crevasses, with grey rock ribs on either side and a dark pine-dusted ridge rising at the top. At the lower middle, at the snowfield's foot, a single large blue ice cave mouth about thirty metres wide opens under a thick arched ice roof, translucent turquoise at its edges; from it a thick plume of white steam pours upward and drifts across the slope, and a warm, faintly green-tinted stream runs from its mouth over grey stones and scree, braiding through bare rock, with a bright melt-band of dark wet ground either side. At the base: bare rock, scree, and a few stunted pines clinging to the ledges. Human trace only at the very edge: a small cairn and a tiny timber bottling hut with a grey roof on a flat shelf by the stream, three tiny alchemists with carrying poles and jars, a narrow zigzag trail climbing in from the lower left. The ice roof of the cave is visibly thin along one lip with a fresh broken block lying below. Light and season: clear cold dawn, golden light from the upper left raking across the snow, long soft blue shadows to the lower right, steam lit gold.

places.name: Hồ Tâm Thang
places.size: A cold mountain lake about 6 km across with a rocky islet about 300 m long at its heart carrying a staircase of about 14 mineral terrace pools; at most a couple of tiny rowing boats and a mooring post.
places.where: Region 1, a high mountain lake of the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác. On the map a bay or lake of dark blue water ringed by snowy and forested slopes, with a dark brown rocky islet in the middle and another rocky island at the top. Hot spring (Water, Fire) held by Thúy Vi. Nearest: Kê Quan Khoáng 90 km, Hồng Lô Cốc 152 km.
places.imagined: A still early winter afternoon. The islet is a steaming white and rust-orange staircase of pools in a dark lake, with an open ring of water around it while the rest is skinned with ice; disciples row out to sit one to a pool.
places.subject: The place: Hồ Tâm Thang, the Hot Spring at the Lake's Heart, a small rocky islet with mineral terraces in the middle of a cold mountain lake. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a dark cold lake fills the frame, ringed by snowy slopes and dark pine, thin ice skinning the water near the shores, and in the middle a small rocky islet about three hundred metres long. Around the islet a ring of open dark water stays unfrozen while the rest of the lake has a pale ice margin and jagged cracks. The islet: its side facing the camera is a staircase of white and rust-orange mineral terraces, some fourteen of them, each a small steaming turquoise pool with a crisp curved rim of sinter, stepping down to the water, the pools linked by thin cascades, steam rising from each in separate plumes that merge above the islet; the top of the islet has a few stunted pines and a flat rock. The lake colours at the foot of the terraces blur from turquoise to deep blue. Signature element: the terraces, bright white and rust and turquoise, are the only warm colours in the frame. Human trace only: two tiny rowing boats on the lake, one pulled up on the islet's pebble landing, a mooring post, and three or four tiny figures sitting singly in separate pools. Light and season: early winter afternoon, golden light from the upper left lighting the steam and the terraces, long soft blue shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Đoản Vĩ Cương
places.size: A rocky lynx ridge about 20 km long, with a hidden robbers' camp of about 25 huts and tents among the rocks, around 60 people, which feeds on the charcoal and tea villages below; the camp is small beside the ridge.
places.where: Region 1, middle cape of Tuyết Hỏa Giác. Temperate forest at about 550 m; on the map a grey-white rocky ridge with scree running through dense dark conifer forest, the sea at the upper left. Beast lair, lynxes, the Ridge of the Bobtails; the robber chief Khấu Thiên Tứ's band hides here, and Vụ Ẩn Môn exists because of it. Nearest: Thái Dược Thôn 79 km, Nhạn Hồi Phong 135 km.
places.imagined: Late afternoon on a bare grey ridge above a dark forest. A few smokes rise from the rocks, a lookout stands on a boulder, bobtailed lynxes watch from ledges, and a line of mules comes up from the villages with sacks of rice.
places.subject: The place: Đoản Vĩ Cương, the Ridge of the Bobtails, a rocky lynx ridge that hides a robbers' camp. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a broad grey-white rocky ridge of broken scree, tors and limestone ribs runs diagonally across the frame, rising out of an ocean of dense dark conifer forest that fills the rest, the sea showing as a pale turquoise edge at the upper left corner. Narrow mule paths run in from the forest at the lower left and right, thin pale lines through the trees. The camp: tucked in a hollow among the rocks about halfway along the ridge, invisible from the sea, about twenty-five low huts of stone and turf roofed with grey bark and brush, canvas lean-tos and a horse corral of rough poles holding about twenty horses, a communal fire with a thin smoke thread, drying racks of meat, a lookout post of piled stones on the highest boulder, rope ladders and a hidden gully path; every roof is camouflaged to match the stone. Signature element: the lynxes, a dozen tiny tawny cats with short bobbed tails and tufted ears, sitting on ledges and crags along the ridge, watching, their markings echoing the dappled rock; the camp lies under their gaze. Life at scale: tiny armed figures at the lookout and the corral, a mule train labouring up the forest path with sacks, a child feeding a horse. Light and season: late afternoon in autumn, golden light from the upper left striking the pale rocks, the forest in deep blue-green shadow, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Mê Vụ Lâm
places.size: A forest about 40 km across lost in drifting mist, training ground of the mist-gate sect; no buildings except a few tiny marker cairns and one lantern post at a crossing, a small hut at most.
places.where: Region 1, middle cape of Tuyết Hỏa Giác. Temperate forest at about 190 m; on the map an unbroken dark forest with a thin river winding down from a small blue bay at the upper right and a few pale marsh pools at the lower left. The Forest of Lost Mist, the training ground of Vụ Ẩn Môn. Nearest: Tất Thụ Thôn 79 km, Du Thụ Lâm 225 km.
places.imagined: Morning, thick low mist. The forest tops show as dark islands in a pale sea, a thin river winds out of it, and in one gap a single lantern glows where a mist-layer is walking trainees round the lost road.
places.subject: The place: Mê Vụ Lâm, the Forest of Lost Mist, a deep forest of the cape drowned in drifting mist. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; an unbroken forest of black pine and spruce fills the frame to every edge, rolling gently, drowned in drifting white-blue mist so that the lower hollows are completely filled with fog while the tree crowns on the rises stand out as dark islands and ridges; a thin silver river winds through from the upper right where a small bay shows, with pale marsh pools and reed pockets at the lower left. The mist is not uniform: it moves in banks, shaped like long wandering ribbons laid along the valleys, with a few deliberate-looking smooth drifts that follow the river. Signature element: in the middle of the frame, a small clearing like a gap in the mist holds a single lantern post and a ring of low marker cairns around a crossing of two narrow forest roads, with a long line of nine tiny trainees in grey walking blindfolded in single file behind a figure carrying a lantern, the mist closing behind them; one more lantern glows far off deep in the fog. Nothing else built; a very small thatched hut by the river is the only roof. Life at scale: the line of trainees, a stag at the river, a few birds above the mist. Light and season: early morning in late autumn, soft golden light from the upper left filtering into the mist, turning the banks pearl and honey, long soft shadows from the treetops to the lower right.

places.name: Vụ Ẩn Môn
places.size: A neutral minor sect of about 35 road guards, lantern-keepers and stonecutters, founded 1050: a compound of about 40 buildings in black-pine forest within about 200 m, ringed by a belt of mist lanterns on poles; small, deliberately plain and hard to see.
places.where: Region 1, middle of the cape Tuyết Hỏa Giác. Temperate forest at about 40 m, black pine with grassy rises; on the map a dense conifer forest with a thin river on the left and a pale rocky ridge at the right. Vassal of Thúy Vi Tông, neutral, Wood 46 %, Water 17 %. Nearest: Hắc Tùng Lâm 152 km, Trà Viên Thôn 152 km. It lays mist over the cape's roads.
places.imagined: Dawn. Mist lies thick in the pines so only the gate lanterns and a few grey roof ridges show, and a carter with a rice-payment is being led down a road that vanishes into moving fog.
places.subject: The place: Vụ Ẩn Môn, the Gate Hidden in Mist, a guild of road guards who lay mist over the cape's roads. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a dense black-pine forest fills the frame with a thin river winding at the left edge and a pale rocky ridge at the right; low drifting mist lies in banks between the trees, thick over the middle of the picture and thinning to the edges, so that the compound is half hidden. The compound: about forty low buildings of dark timber and fieldstone with grey tile roofs set among the pines on a gentle rise, with no long straight walls but a ring of pine-log palisade broken by trees; a plain gate hall with two lanterns, a long guard barracks, a stone yard with stonecutters' sheds and cut blocks, a lantern-keeping hall with racks of hundreds of hanging lanterns, a small shrine, kitchens and stables for about twenty horses. Signature element: a wide belt of tall wooden lantern poles, each with a small round lantern glowing amber, stands around and outward from the compound along every approaching road, perhaps two hundred of them, and the mist drifts in a visible slow spiral around the compound and out along the roads, a pale bank following the four tracks outward like roots; where the mist lies the roads can be seen only as faint lines. Life at scale: tiny grey-clad guards walking a patrol with lanterns, a carter with a laden cart paying a handful of rice at the outer gate, stonecutters at a block. Light and season: dawn in late autumn, pale golden light from the upper left breaking through the pines, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Thúy Vi Tông (the Cliff Hall)
places.size: The old seat of a great sect, abandoned as headquarters in 1001-1006 and now the Cliff Hall: still a domain about 4 km across on twin summits, with roughly 250 buildings and kilometres of terraces, but now kept by a grand elder, a steward and a few dozen others; the herb terraces are partly kept, partly overgrown. It once held thousands.
places.where: Region 3, the north-western hills on a high Metal ridge at about 1.5 km elevation, temperate forest. On the map a rugged grey and white rocky mountain land of ridges and scree among dark forest, two high summits close together at the centre. The founder's seat of Thúy Vi Tông (alchemy, Metal 38 %), now the Cliff Hall with the founder's grave, the founder's pine and the old life trees; the sect's court moved down to Cổ Dịch Trấn. Nearest: Bích Ngọc Khoáng mine 127 km, Quy Tịch Phong peak 141 km.
places.imagined: A misty morning above the haze. Twin summits stand out of blue-green cloud, a broad white stone path spirals up the higher one, and the halls are mostly quiet; smoke rises from only a few chimneys, and one ancient pine stands alone at the founder's grave.
places.subject: The place: Thúy Vi Tông's old seat, now the Cliff Hall, a great alchemist sect's former headquarters on twin summits. Setting: seen from very high above at a steep aerial angle; two high steep summits rise side by side out of a sea of blue-green haze that fills the valleys below them, their slopes forested in dark green and flushed grey where bare Metal-rich rock shows through, ridges and scree running off in all directions to the frame edges. The seat: roughly two hundred and fifty white-walled halls under green-glazed roofs, tall stacked pagoda halls, galleries and gate towers, built on stepped terraces that climb both peaks, palace-sized halls on the upper shelves and long dormitory ranges below, connected by covered stairs, bridges over ravines and a cliff-hanging lift of rope; the slopes between are stepped with herb terraces in green stripes, a few of them tidy and cut, many gone to tall grass and young pines. Signature element: around the higher summit a broad path of white stone winds in a spiral from the haze at the foot to the peak, its pale upper turns visible above the cloud, with the sect's tallest pagoda at the top; on a high shelf between the two summits a single huge ancient pine stands alone beside a small stone-walled grave enclosure, with a ring of old life trees around it, the only dense green. The quiet is the point: only a handful of chimneys smoke, many halls are shuttered with moss on their tile edges, courtyards bare and swept in only a few places, and tiny figures are scarce: a dozen in grey carrying water on the white path, one at the grave. Light and season: misty early morning, soft golden light from the upper left on the summits, haze glowing blue-green in the valleys, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Vân Khởi Quán
places.size: A Daoist abbey of about 40 monks, novices and lay brothers, founded 540: about 30 small grey stone halls stepping up a mountain shoulder over some 500 m, with one slim two-roofed hall as its tallest; small, quiet and high.
places.where: Region 3, high on the Metal heights above Thúy Vi's old ridge. High mountain at about 880 m; on the map a ridge of forest, grey rock and scree running beside a wide blue sea or inlet at the right, with another bay at the lower left. Vassal of Thúy Vi Tông, righteous. Nearest: Vân Mẫu Khoáng mine 79 km, Thủy Cùng Phong peak 79 km. Founded by Tống Tọa Vân, last student of Không Sơn Viện, still its abbot.
places.imagined: Clouds rising from the valleys at evening, a thin stream threading up past the grey halls to a cleft where it vanishes, and a wooden platform juting out over the drop where novices sit and watch.
places.subject: The place: Vân Khởi Quán, the Abbey of Rising Clouds, a small mountain abbey of hermits and teachers. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a high rocky shoulder of grey stone, scree and dark conifer fills the frame, a wide blue sea at the right edge far below, valley clouds rolling up the slope from the lower right as white banks and gaps. The abbey: about thirty small halls of grey stone with dark grey tile roofs stepping up the slope in a staggered line beside a thin silver stream, small courtyards and a gate, a long plain refectory, cells for monks in rows, a sutra hall, a herb plot behind a low stone wall, and, at the top, a slim two-roofed hall the abbey's tallest outline; stone stairs link everything and a little footbridge crosses the stream. Signature element: the stream leads uphill past the halls and vanishes into a narrow cleft in the rock; beside that spot a cantilevered wooden platform juts out over the cliff edge, with a dozen tiny figures in grey sitting in a row on it, looking out at the clouds rising from the valleys below; the clouds are climbing the cliff and about to wet the platform. Life at scale: a monk sweeping a stair, two carrying water, a line of novices on the steps, a thin smoke from the kitchen. Light and season: evening in autumn, golden light from the upper left on the grey roofs, cool blue shadows in the clefts, long soft shadows to the lower right, the clouds glowing white and rose.

places.name: Hàn Tân Thành
places.size: A walled port city of about 14,000 roofs and some 70,000 people, walls about 2.4 km by 1.8 km, on both banks' approach to a wide shallow ford; it is a city of fishers and ferrymen with long quays and a line of lamp pillars about 1.5 km long across the river.
places.where: Region 1 / north coast. Tundra at sea level where a broad river meets the sea, the northern ford and port of the cold coast; on the map a deep blue bay on the left with a rocky islet, dark forest on the right and a thin river joining the bay from the upper right. Thúy Vi Tông city, once under Không Sơn Viện, changed hands twice. Nearest: Lãnh Sam Lâm forest 90 km, Lô Khẩu Trấn ruin 160 km.
places.imagined: The first night of the Cold Ford lamps. Every pillar across the shallow ford has its niche glowing, lamps on every boat, and the grey city lies behind them in the cold dusk.
places.subject: The place: Hàn Tân Thành, the Cold Ford city, a walled port at a shallow river ford on a bleak northern coast. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; flat pale tundra and dark scrub forest fill the right half, a broad river enters from the upper right and spreads into a shallow braided ford before meeting the sea, a blue-grey bay filling the left half with a rocky islet and thin ice at the shore. The city: a rectangular wall of grey stone about two and a half kilometres long with gate towers and a squat gate tower the tallest roof, enclosing some fourteen thousand grey-tile roofs in dense blocks: a ferrymen's quarter at the ford with stables and wagon yards, a fishers' district with smokehouses and net lofts, a central market and a plain lord's hall, canals and bridges, long stone quays; boats of all sizes fill the harbour, with ferry barges lined up at the ford. Signature element: a line of tall stone pillars, about eighty of them, crosses the river ford from bank to bank in a long straight line a kilometre and a half long, each pillar with a small glowing lamp niche, a bead of gold in a grey line, marking the safe crossing for wagons and boats; a long wagon train is crossing alongside it with tiny torches. Life at scale: lamp-lit boats, ferry crews, lines of carts, small crowds on the quay. Light and season: first night of winter at dusk, last golden light from the upper left on the walls, the lamps strong against the deep blue shadows, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Lam Yên Thị
places.size: A market built along a broad stone stair about 1.2 km long, with roughly 500 stalls under indigo awnings, a few storehouses at its foot and perhaps 400 permanent houses and inns along the sides; a market of perhaps 3,000 residents and many more visitors, not a city.
places.where: Region 3, below Thúy Vi Tông's old seat: temperate forest at about 180 m, on forested slopes rising to a rocky Metal ridge; on the map dense forest slopes running down to a blue bay in the upper left, with grey bare rocky ridges to the south. Thúy Vi Tông market. Nearest: Dưỡng Mộc Tuyền spirit vein 79 km, Cổ Dịch Trấn 182 km. Herbs, pill ingredients, scripture.
places.imagined: A misty market day. The two lines of stalls under deep indigo awnings climb the stair and fade step by step into blue-green haze, each hung with a small bell so customers can find their stall in the mist.
places.subject: The place: Lam Yên Thị, the Haze Market, a market laid along a broad stone stair below a mountain sect. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a forested mountain slope of dark green conifer rises across the frame from lower left to upper right into a layer of blue-green haze, a bay of the sea showing at the upper left, grey rocky ridges at the lower right. The market: a broad stone stair, about twenty metres wide, climbs the slope in long straight flights with landings, from a flat yard at the foot where about thirty low grey-roofed storehouses, a carters' yard with wagons and an inn quarter stand, up through the forest; along both sides run two continuous lines of stalls, some five hundred of them, under deep indigo cloth awnings, each hung with a small bell, with taller buildings of timber and grey tile, inns, scripture shops, pill-ingredient warehouses, tea houses, behind them on the slope; the awnings fade step by step into the mist toward the top so that the upper flights show as faint blue ghosts and finally only as a pale line. Signature element: the indigo awning lines, two long dark-blue ribbons climbing into haze, the single most striking colour in the picture. Life at scale: hundreds of tiny shoppers and porters on the stair, carters with ox wagons at the foot, a group of scholars at a bookmark stall, herbalists with baskets. Light and season: misty late-autumn morning, soft golden light from the upper left on the lower stalls, haze glowing blue-green above, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Bách Diệp Trấn
places.size: A small walled river-mouth town of about 1,100 roofs inside a wall about 450 m by 350 m, roughly 5,000 people, with a small wooden harbour, at the centre of a grid of several thousand cypresses about 5 km across.
places.where: Region 3, on the coast at a river mouth, sea level. Temperate forest; on the map a deep blue bay at the right and below, a river entering from a grey bare ridge at the upper left, forested slopes at both sides. Thúy Vi Tông town. Nearest: Kỳ Bàn Phong peak 112 km. The cypresses were planted by students of Không Sơn Viện in 240.
places.imagined: A calm noon. Dark spire-shaped cypresses march out from the town in perfectly straight lines in every direction, and the town sits at the centre of the pattern like a hub.
places.subject: The place: Bách Diệp Trấn, the Hundred Cypress town, a river-mouth town set in a vast grid of ancient cypresses. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a deep blue bay fills the right and lower part of the frame, a river enters from a grey rocky ridge at the upper left and spreads in a sandy delta, and the land beyond is forested slope. The town: a small rectangular walled town about four hundred and fifty metres long, grey stone walls, with some eleven hundred grey-tile roofs in straight streets, a gate tower on the land side, a small wooden harbour with a pier and two dozen small boats, a resin and incense warehouse row, a central square, a sandy bank for boats. Signature element: surrounding the town on the land side is a large, exact grid of tall dark spire-shaped cypresses, several thousand of them, planted in perfectly straight rows with measured spacing, running out five kilometres and filling the land to the frame edges, so that the dark columns march away from the town in lines; avenues of bare ground run between them in a crossed pattern, and the town sits at the centre like the hub of the pattern. Tiny cart tracks follow the avenues. Life at scale: resin tappers with buckets at a few trees, tiny figures on the avenues, smoke from incense kilns, a seedling nursery as a patch of small green dots. Light and season: noon in early autumn, warm golden light from the upper left, each cypress casting a narrow shadow toward the lower right in a repeating pattern.

places.name: Tiều Ca Trấn
places.size: A small walled timber town of about 1,000 roofs on a narrow coastal strip, a wall about 400 m by 300 m, roughly 4,500 people, with a log flume about 3 km long from the ridge top to the harbour; an industrial town, with timber yards.
places.where: Region 3, west coast at sea level, temperate forest; on the map a dark deep sea along the left and lower edge, a steep forested coastal strip with a patchwork of small fields in the lower middle. Thúy Vi Tông town below Không Sơn Viện. Nearest: Hồi Âm Cốc gorge 79 km. Woodcutters were asked to sing more quietly below the academy.
places.imagined: A working morning. Logs rattle down the long flume from the ridge into the log pond, the woodcutters on the ridges sing, and a cargo boat waits at the short pier.
places.subject: The place: Tiều Ca Trấn, the Woodcutters' Song town, a walled timber town on a narrow coast below steep forested ridges. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a dark deep sea runs down the left side with white surf lines, a narrow coastal strip of small field pockets and grass runs along it, and steep forested ridges rise to the right and upper edge, bare pockets of felled slope visible high on them. The town: a small rectangular walled town about four hundred metres long, built mostly of timber with grey tile roofs, about a thousand roofs, with a gate tower, a main street running down to the harbour, sawyers' halls, shingle makers, cooperages, boat yards and a woodcutters' guildhall; beyond the wall a large timber yard with stacks of squared logs and a log pond. Signature element: a long raised wooden log flume, a V-shaped timber trough on trestles about three kilometres long, runs from the ridge top straight down the slope into the harbour, its upper reaches lost in forest, with logs visible in it as tiny dark dashes, spray at its joints, and a splash where it enters the log pond; a short pier with a cargo boat stacked with timber waits beyond. Life at scale: woodcutters as tiny specks along the ridge singing and felling, teamsters with oxen, children running along the trestles. Light and season: bright morning in early autumn, golden light from the upper left on the flume and the timber stacks, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Ô Đề Thôn
places.size: A fishing village of about 30 grey-roofed houses on a strip of shore, perhaps 150 people, with a single huge bare oak (about 30 m tall) on the ridge above; all in about 250 m.
places.where: Region 3, west coast at sea level, temperate forest; on the map a wooded peninsula with a deep inlet and a river joining from the upper right. Thúy Vi Tông village. Nearest: Lão Tượng Lâm forest 75 km. Crows gathered here in 410.
places.imagined: A grey dawn. Hundreds of crows crowd the bare oak on the ridge top against the pale sky, and the fishers look up at it before they launch.
places.subject: The place: Ô Đề Thôn, the Crow Landing, a small fishing village under a long ridge crowned by one huge bare oak. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a long wooded ridge runs across the upper frame, dark conifer and grey rock, with a strip of pebble shore below it and the grey-blue sea in the lower third, a wooded headland to the left. The village: about thirty grey-tile houses on the narrow strip of shore, in a double line along a lane, with fish-drying racks, net lofts, boat sheds and a stone slipway, a dozen boats drawn up on a pebble beach. Signature element: on the very top of the ridge stands one huge leafless oak, the oldest tree for miles, thirty metres tall, its black branches spreading like a cracked bowl against the pale sky, and its branches thickly dotted with hundreds of black crows as specks, with more crows circling above it and a thin stream of them leaving along the ridge; a faint track climbs from the village to its foot, where a small heap of grain offerings lies. The sea below the shingle is calm, with a thin fringe of foam, and the village lane is dark with frost. Life at scale: three or four tiny fishers looking up from the boats, nets on the racks, a child scattering grain on the track, smoke from two chimneys. Light and season: cold early dawn in winter, pale gold light from the upper left lighting the oak's branches, long soft shadows toward the lower right, the sea grey.

places.name: Lâm Tuyền Thôn
places.size: A coastal village of about 35 grey-roofed houses, perhaps 180 people, with a bamboo pipe line about 1 km long and a row of 8 stone troughs; in a space of about 300 m.
places.where: Region 3, west coast at sea level, temperate forest; on the map a wooded peninsula beside a deep sea, a pale cultivated patch at the lower right. Thúy Vi Tông village. Nearest: Thiền Minh Lâm forest 79 km. A spring in the woods cured the coughing sickness of 760.
places.imagined: A bright morning. Split bamboo pipes on wooden trestles run down from the woods and end in a row of stone troughs in the square, always running, with travellers filling jars.
places.subject: The place: Lâm Tuyền Thôn, the Wood Spring village, a coastal village fed by a long bamboo pipe line. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; wooded slopes of mixed green forest fill the upper half, the deep blue sea with white surf the left, small field pockets in yellow and green at the lower right, a path running into the woods. The village: about thirty-five grey-tile houses along two lanes by the shore, each with a small yard and a vegetable plot, a few boats drawn up, a small square with a plain well-house and a shrine of a single roof. Signature element: a long line of split bamboo pipes, about a kilometre of them, runs down from the woods on wooden trestles of varying height, each family's length marked by its own repaired joints, dipping and rising over the slope, and ends in a row of eight stone troughs in the village square, water spilling silver from each and glinting, always running; a few jars on the troughs' edges, a queue of travellers with carrying poles. Spring-green moss and a ribbon of ferns trace the pipe line through the trees. The bamboo pipes are pale green-gold where fresh and silver-grey where old, and their shadows lie in thin stripes across the moss. Life at scale: women washing at the troughs, a boy fixing a joint on a trestle, two cultivators resting under a tree, fishing boats at the shore. Light and season: bright early summer morning, golden light from the upper left, the water sparkling, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Thu Diệp Thôn
places.size: A small shore village of about 25 grey-roofed houses, perhaps 120 people, in front of a maple grove about 400 m across; in a space of about 250 m.
places.where: Region 3, west coast at sea level, a rocky green headland; on the map a wooded peninsula with a grey rocky ridge, a deep blue sea on both sides and a small island at the lower left. Thúy Vi Tông village. Nearest: Hồng Phong Đỉnh peak 285 km. Red leaves sold at Lam Yên Thị as scripture bookmarks, only mortals may gather them.
places.imagined: Peak autumn. A grove of red maples burns crimson behind the village, the brightest red on the coast, and wooden frames of pressed leaves dry in rows along the house walls.
places.subject: The place: Thu Diệp Thôn, the Autumn Leaf village, a shore village in front of a crimson maple grove. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a green wooded headland with a grey rocky ridge runs up the frame's centre, the deep blue sea on both sides with white surf along the rocks, a small wooded islet at the lower left. The village: about twenty-five grey-tile houses along a footpath on the shore side of the grove, with small yards, a boat landing with a single boat, a plain communal press-house and a shrine of one small roof. Signature element: a dense grove of red maples about four hundred metres across, in full crimson, the brightest red on the whole coast, spread behind the village against the dark green of the surrounding trees; along the house walls stand rows of small wooden leaf-pressing frames, each holding a stack of pressed red leaves between boards, and a few long drying lines of single leaves hung out like red flags; fallen leaves scatter a red carpet over the path and the shore. The path between the grove and the shore is deep in leaves, and the maple crowns glow so strongly that the nearby roofs are tinted rose. Life at scale: a dozen tiny villagers gathering leaves in baskets under the trees, a girl pressing a leaf, a boat on the water, smoke from three chimneys. Light and season: peak autumn afternoon, warm golden light from the upper left setting the maples aglow, long soft shadows toward the lower right.

places.name: Bích Ngọc Khoáng
places.size: An open stepped quarry cut into a forested hill, about 600 m wide and 250 m high, with a zigzag cart ramp, two tiny sheds and spoil heaps; a working face of a few hundred people at most, small beside the mountains.
places.where: Region 3, a green mountain at about 1,000 m, temperate forest; on the map rugged grey and white ridges and scree among dark forest, with tiny blue tarns. Jade mine (hàn ngọc; Metal, Earth) worked by Hồng Lô Cốc under Thúy Vi. Nearest: Quy Tịch Phong peak 79 km, Thúy Vi Tông 127 km. Opened 505.
places.imagined: Afternoon sun on a stepped quarry face banded with bright jade-green stone, a cart ramp zigzagging down its middle to the road, a few carts waiting at the foot.
places.subject: The place: Bích Ngọc Khoáng, the Green Jade Mine, a stepped open quarry cut into a forested mountain. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a high green mountain of dark conifer forest and grey rock ribs fills the frame, small blue tarns glinting between the ridges. The quarry: a large amphitheatre of stepped terraced faces, about thirty benches each a few metres high, cut into the side of a forested hill, the cut faces showing bands of bright jade-green stone, pale and dark, stacked in layers like a green-striped cake; down the middle a zigzag cart ramp of packed earth descends in some fifteen switchbacks to a road at the foot. At the foot: spoil heaps of grey and green chips, two tiny plain sheds with grey roofs, a few carts waiting, a pale road winding off through the forest toward the lower left. Signature element: the green-banded stepped quarry face with its zigzag ramp, vivid jade against the darker forest. Life at scale: tiny miners in rows on the benches with picks, a mule cart descending the ramp, a few figures at the sheds loading blocks. Light and season: clear afternoon in early autumn, warm golden light from the upper left on the green terraces, long soft shadows toward the lower right. The quarry's benches are cut with precise square corners, so that the pale cut faces and the dark forest above them make a bold geometric shape on the hillside, and a thin drain channel runs down from its upper lip. Below the road at the foot a stack of rough-squared jade blocks waits on timber skids beside a heap of crushed green chips. Pines and moss crowd the quarry's edges, and a pale cart track climbs back into the hills.

places.name: Vân Mẫu Khoáng
places.size: A bare slope with one dark mine mouth about 8 m wide and a fan of mica tailings about 500 m long; no buildings, a narrow path and perhaps a tiny shed.
places.where: Region 3, high mountain at about 430 m on a ridge by the coast; on the map a grey rocky mountain with forest on its flanks, a stream running into a blue bay at the right. Mica mine (huyền hoàng thạch; Metal, Wood) worked by the monks of Vân Khởi Quán. Nearest: Vân Khởi Quán 79 km. Opened 560.
places.imagined: Sunlight on a bare grey slope; a wide fan of glittering silver mica spills from a dark mine mouth like a cloud resting on the rock, and a lone monk digs a little for the lesson.
places.subject: The place: Vân Mẫu Khoáng, the Cloud-Mother Mine, a bare slope with one mine mouth and a fan of glittering mica. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a bare grey mountain slope of broken rock and scree fills the frame, with dark conifer forest on its lower flanks at the left, a thin stream running down at the upper right to a wide blue bay at the right edge. Signature element: from one dark mine mouth about eight metres wide high on the slope spills a wide fan of silver-white mica tailings, about five hundred metres long and widening as it descends, glittering with thousands of tiny sparks like a cloud resting on the rock, its edges fading into the grey scree; faint pale sheets of mica catch the light on the cliff above in thin bright seams. At the base: scree and a narrow path winding down, a small cairn, and a tiny shelter with a grey roof near the foot. Human trace: two tiny monks in grey with baskets near the mine mouth and one with a pick, and a mule with panniers on the path. No other buildings. Light and season: clear afternoon in autumn, strong golden light from the upper left making the mica sparkle, cool blue shadows in the clefts, long soft shadows toward the lower right. The mica fan's edges break into rounded lobes where each rainstorm has pushed the tailings further down, and a few thin silver rivulets of meltwater run through it, flashing. Above the mine mouth a cap of dark overhanging rock throws a hard black shadow, and a ladder of pale cut steps leads up to a small ledge where the monks sort the sheets. The path below is marked by a line of small cairns toward a distant ridge.

places.name: Không Sơn Viện
places.size: A ruined academy of about 60 grey stone halls and pavilions on a high ridge over about 800 m, once a school of several hundred; abandoned and empty since its last master gave the hills away in 500, never looted, doors open. Quiet, not burned.
places.where: Region 3, high mountain at about 1.6 km, temperate forest below; on the map a rugged ridge of grey rock and scree among dark forest descending to a blue bay at the lower middle, a thin river running down the left. Former sect (Metal, Earth), left empty after its master gave the hills to Thúy Vi's founder; the sect keeps it untouched. Nearest: Lăng Không Đỉnh peak 79 km. Founded 180.
places.imagined: Dawn above the haze. The ridge halls stand silent with their doors open, the great lecture hall's roof sagging, a pagoda missing its top tier, a raw landslide scar beside the path with a half-buried stone gate carved with poetry.
places.subject: The place: Không Sơn Viện, the Academy of the Empty Mountain, a ruin of broken verticals on a high ridge above the mist. Setting: seen from high above at a steep aerial angle; a rugged bare ridge of grey rock and scree runs across the frame among dark conifer forest, a layer of pale mist filling the valley at the lower left with a thin river running out of it, and a blue bay far below at the bottom. The ruin: about sixty old academy halls of grey stone with weathered grey tile roofs arranged on terraces along the ridge crest, small courtyards, covered corridors, a double gate, and student cells in rows; every door stands open, some roofs have slipped, grass and small pines grow in the courtyards and between flagstones; a great lecture hall at the centre with its roof sagging at one end and its ridge dipped, and next to it a small pagoda missing its top roofs, its stump broken. Nothing is burned and nothing looted: the buildings stand whole but empty and tidy, with swept steps. Signature element: a raw brown landslide scar runs down the slope beside the approach path, and in it a stone gate carved with fine lines of poetry stands half buried, its pillars tilted, one lintel exposed, the only thing out of order. Human trace: a single tiny traveller sitting on the steps of the lecture hall and one more at the half-buried gate; no smoke. Light and season: cold clear dawn, golden light from the upper left on the grey stone and the pale mist, long soft shadows toward the lower right.
